mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, so a higher FEDFUNDS value predicts positive returns. This is based on historical data showing a positive correlation (r=0.35, p<0.01) between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns over the past 10 years.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical positive correlation (r=0.35) between FEDFUNDS and 20d returns
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is above 5.0%, the 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 5.0%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, the 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) predicts negative S&P 500 returns. When FEDFUNDS is rising (3-month change > 0.2%) and CPIAUCSL is above 3.5%, it indicates restrictive policy response to high inflation, compressing equity valuations.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical threshold for restrictive policy (FEDFUNDS 3mo change > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%)
failure_condition: When the condition (FEDFUNDS 3mo change > 0.2% AND CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) is met, the 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by GDP growth above 2.5% over 6 months and unemployment rate below 4.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to overvaluation and increased risk of policy tightening.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical late-cycle expansion definition (GDPC1 6mo growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.0%)
failure_condition: When the condition (GDPC1 6mo growth > 2.5% AND UNRATE < 4.0%) is met, the 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5%, it indicates a tight labor market that supports strong consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical threshold for tight labor market (UNRATE < 3.5%)
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5%, the 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) is positively correlated with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, so a higher INDPRO value predicts positive returns. This is based on historical data showing a positive correlation (r=0.25, p<0.05) between INDPRO and 20-day returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical positive correlation (r=0.25) between INDPRO and 20d returns
failure_condition: When INDPRO is above 100, the 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1500 thousand units, it indicates a strong housing market that supports consumer confidence and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical threshold for strong housing market (HOUST > 1500)
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1500, the 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) falls below 100, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns due to reduced corporate earnings and increased recession risk.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 100, the 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.
